name: Uldor

claims.text: After entering Beleriand, Uldor along with his father and his brothers joined the service of Caranthir, and settled in Thargelion.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of the Ruin of Beleriand and the Fall of Fingolfin"; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part Two. The Later Quenta Silmarillion: Of Beleriand its Realms (Chapter 11)","Sheet 2: North-east", p. 183

claims.text: Ultimately though, his father Ulfang's purpose from the beginning was to eventually betray the Elves, which his sons ultimately did in the Battle of Unnumbered Tears, under Uldor's leadership - they turned against their allies, attacking them in the rear. Their betrayal proved crucial in the fight against Morgoth's forces, though, and Morgoth was victorious.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part One. The Grey Annals": §174, pp. 60-1, footnote; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of the Fifth Battle: Nirnaeth Arnoediad"

claims.text: However, Uldor's brothers Ulfast and Ulwarth were killed by the sons of Bór, who remained loyal to the sons of Fëanor during the battle - while Uldor himself was slain by Maglor.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of the Fifth Battle: Nirnaeth Arnoediad"

claims.text: According to earlier versions of the legendarium, instead of being killed by Maglor in the Battle of Unnumbered Tears, Uldor was slain by Cranthir (an earlier name for Caranthir) instead.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "VII. The Earliest Annals of Beleriand: [The first version of The Earliest Annals of Beleriand (Text AB I)]", entry 172, p. 302; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, "Part Two: Valinor and Middle-earth before The Lord of the Rings, III. The Later Annals of Beleriand", entry 272, p. 137
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Earlier versions of the Nirnaeth

claims.text: It is only in The Grey Annals (c. 1951) that the story of Uldor's death at Maglor's hand appears, as well as the idea that Uldor summoned more Men from east of Beleriand.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part One. The Grey Annals": §231, entry 472, p. 74; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part One. The Grey Annals": Note on §231, p. 134
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Earlier versions of the Nirnaeth

claims.text: And while the idea of the treachery of the Easterlings was retained, it was only mentioned in passing.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The War of the Jewels, "Part One. The Grey Annals","Note 2 (A further account of the Battle of Unnumbered Tears)", pp. 165-8
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Later legendarium

claims.text: In the appendix of The Lost Road and Other Writings in The Genealogies (dating from the early 1930s), it is stated that Uldor was born in the year 125.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, "Appendix: I. The Genealogies", p. 403
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Uldor's year of birth

claims.text: When comparing the above date with its associated text The Earliest Annals of Beleriand, Uldor was born 38 years before the Swarthy Men entered Beleriand in the year 163.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "VII. The Earliest Annals of Beleriand: [The first version of The Earliest Annals of Beleriand (Text AB I)]", entry year 163, p. 300
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Uldor's year of birth

claims.text: Also, the dates found in The Earliest Annals of Beleriand were by and large moved 300 years into the future in The Grey Annals (c. early 1950s), such that, for example, an event happening in the year 195 in The Earliest Annals now happened in the year .
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "VII. The Earliest Annals of Beleriand: Commentary on the Annals of Beleriand (text AB I)", Annals 155 to 157, pp. 319-20
